title: Eisenstein Conjecture for cos(π/p), General Odd Prime p
description: States the uniform Eisenstein conjecture: for every odd prime p ≥ 3, the minimal polynomial of 2 + 2cos(π/p) over ℚ is Eisenstein at p. Defines a parametric polynomial r : ℕ → ℤ[X] with explicit values for p ∈ {5, 7, 11, 13}: r₅ = Y²−5Y+5, r₇ = Y³−7Y²+14Y−7, r₁₁ = Y⁵−11Y⁴+44Y³−77Y²+55Y−11, r₁₃ = Y⁶−13Y⁵+65Y⁴−156Y³+182Y²−91Y+13. Proves IsEisensteinAt for each of the four primes by direct coefficient computation, and derives irreducibility for the new primes p = 11, p = 13. The general conjecture is stated as a sorry; the proof requires the cyclotomic-ramification argument that 2 + 2cos(π/p) is a uniformizer in the unique prime above p in ℤ[2cos(π/p)] (totally ramified extension of degree (p−1)/2, with norm Φ_{2p}(−1) = Φ_p(1) = p).

meta.historicalContext: The angle trisection impossibility proof reduces to the irreducibility of minimal polynomials of cosines. For specific primes the gallery already has formalizations: cos(20°) = cos(π/9) (Eisenstein at 3), cos(π/5) (Eisenstein at 5), cos(π/7) (Eisenstein at 7). The pattern Y → Y − 2 and the resulting Eisenstein-at-p form for the minimal polynomial of 2 + 2cos(π/p) is conjectured to hold for every odd prime p ≥ 3. The cyclotomic perspective ties this to Φ_{2p}(−1) = Φ_p(1) = p, a Mathlib-available identity, and the standard ramification theory of cyclotomic fields developed by Kummer, Hilbert, and Hensel.

Each obligation reduces to `decide` or `interval_cases k <;> norm_num` after coefficient unfolding. For p ∈ {11, 13}, derive irreducibility via `Polynomial.irreducible_of_eisenstein_criterion`. General conjecture (sorry): cyclotomic ramification — (1+ζ_{2p}) is uniformizer of unique prime above p in ℤ[ζ_{2p}] (Mathlib's `IsCyclotomicExtension.Rat.totallyRamified`), descends to (2 + 2cos(π/p)) as uniformizer in the real subfield with ramification index (p−1)/2, hence minimal polynomial is Eisenstein by local-field theory.

overview.historicalContext:
The angle trisection impossibility theorem (Wantzel 1837, building on Galois 1830) follows from the fact that cos(20°) has degree 3 over ℚ, since the trisection of 60° would require constructing a cube root via straightedge and compass — provably impossible since constructible numbers have degree a power of 2 over ℚ. The minimal polynomial of cos(20°) is $8X^3 - 6X - 1$, which after the substitution $Y = 2X + 2$ becomes $Y^3 - 6Y^2 + 9Y - 3$, Eisenstein at $p = 3$. This pattern generalizes: for every odd prime $p$, the minimal polynomial of $\cos(\pi/p)$ (equivalently, of $\theta_p = 2\cos(\pi/p)$) has the structurally similar form, and after the substitution $Y = X + 2$ becomes a degree-$(p-1)/2$ monic polynomial in $\mathbb{Z}[Y]$ that is Eisenstein at $p$.

The cyclotomic perspective places this in a unified framework. Let $\zeta = \zeta_{2p} = \exp(i\pi/p)$ be a primitive $2p$-th root of unity. Then $\theta_p = \zeta + \zeta^{-1}$ is a generator of the maximal real subfield $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_{2p})^+$, with $[\mathbb{Q}(\theta_p) : \mathbb{Q}] = (p-1)/2$. The element $2 + \theta_p$ factors as $(1+\zeta)(1+\zeta^{-1})$, and its norm to $\mathbb{Q}$ equals $|\Phi_{2p}(-1)|^2 \cdot \ldots$ — but more directly, using $\Phi_{2p}(X) = \Phi_p(-X)$ for odd primes $p \geq 3$, we have $\Phi_{2p}(-1) = \Phi_p(1) = p$. Hence $N_{\mathbb{Q}(\theta_p)/\mathbb{Q}}(2 + \theta_p) = p$, so the constant term of the minimal polynomial $r_p$ of $2 + \theta_p$ is $\pm p$.

The Eisenstein condition on sub-leading coefficients follows from ramification theory: the prime $p$ is totally ramified in $\mathbb{Z}[\zeta_{2p}]$ with ramification index $\varphi(2p) = p - 1$, and the unique prime above $p$ is generated by $(1 - \zeta_{2p})$ (or equivalently $(1 + \zeta_{2p})$, since $-\zeta$ is also a primitive $2p$-th root). Restricting to the real subfield $\mathbb{Q}(\theta_p)$ halves the ramification index to $(p-1)/2$, and $2 + \theta_p = (1+\zeta)(1+\zeta^{-1})$ becomes a uniformizer of the unique prime $\mathfrak{p}_\theta$ above $p$ in $\mathbb{Z}[\theta_p]$. The standard local-field theorem (Neukirch, *Algebraic Number Theory*, II.6) states that the minimal polynomial of a uniformizer of a totally ramified extension is Eisenstein, completing the unified proof.
overview.problemStatement: For every odd prime p ≥ 3, is the minimal polynomial of 2 + 2cos(π/p) over ℚ Eisenstein at p? Empirically verified for p ∈ {5, 7, 11, 13}; conjecture stated uniformly.
overview.proofStrategy: The file implements Level 2 of the formalization strategy (per the slug's S1 OBSERVE plan in knowledge.md): a parametric definition `r : ℕ → ℤ[X]` with explicit values for p ∈ {5, 7, 11, 13}, per-prime Eisenstein verification by direct coefficient computation, and the uniform conjecture stated as a sorry. The per-prime proofs follow the same template as the sibling files (`AngleTrisectionCos20GalOQ01OQ02.lean` for p=5, `AngleTrisectionCos20GalOQ01.lean` for p=7), applied to the four primes via Lean's `IsEisensteinAt` structure. Irreducibility of the new polynomials r₁₁ and r₁₃ follows via `Polynomial.irreducible_of_eisenstein_criterion`. The general statement remains open pending the cyclotomic-ramification proof, which requires the local-field theorem 'uniformizer of totally ramified extension ⇒ minimal polynomial is Eisenstein' (potentially missing in full generality from Mathlib).
keyInsights: **Uniform polynomial r : ℕ → ℤ[X]**: A single parametric definition with explicit values for the four smallest odd primes p ≥ 5. The structure makes the conjecture statement clean: `∃ q : ℤ[X], q.natDegree = (p−1)/2 ∧ q.Monic ∧ q.IsEisensteinAt (Ideal.span {(p : ℤ)})`.

**Norm identity N(2 + 2cos(π/p)) = p**: Follows from Φ_{2p}(−1) = Φ_p(1) = p for odd primes p ≥ 3. This is the source of the constant term ±p in r_p, and a Mathlib-available identity via `Polynomial.cyclotomic_eq_minpoly` and explicit value computation.

**Uniformizer characterization**: 2 + 2cos(π/p) = (1 + ζ_{2p})(1 + ζ_{2p}⁻¹) is a uniformizer of the unique prime 𝔭_θ above p in ℤ[2cos(π/p)]. The ramification index in the real subfield is (p−1)/2 — exactly the degree of r_p. The 'uniformizer ⇒ Eisenstein minimal polynomial' theorem is the bridge from local field theory to the algebraic conjecture.

**Coefficient computation pattern**: Each per-prime Eisenstein verification reduces to (i) `decide` for leading coefficient 1 ∉ (p), (ii) `interval_cases k <;> norm_num` for sub-leading coefficients in (p), (iii) `decide` for constant term ∉ (p²). The pattern is mechanical and scales to any specific prime.

**Sub-leading coefficients are sums of products of (1+ζᵏ)(1+ζ⁻ᵏ)**: Each elementary symmetric polynomial in the conjugates {2 + 2cos(kπ/p) : k odd, 1 ≤ k ≤ p−2} is a sum of products of terms (1 + ζ^k_{2p})(1 + ζ^{−k}_{2p}), each of which lies in 𝔭_θ (the unique prime above p). Hence each sub-leading coefficient is divisible by p.

**Connection to constructibility**: The degree of r_p is (p−1)/2. For p = 5 this is 2 (constructible), for p = 7 this is 3 (NOT constructible, since 3 is not a power of 2), for p = 11 this is 5, for p = 13 this is 6. This recovers Gauss's regular n-gon constructibility theorem: the regular p-gon is constructible iff p is a Fermat prime (p = 2^(2^k) + 1), i.e., iff (p−1)/2 is a power of 2.

sections.title: Conjecture and Definitions
sections.summary: States the Eisenstein conjecture for cos(π/p), describes the explicit polynomials for p ∈ {5, 7, 11, 13}, sketches the cyclotomic ramification proof, and defines the parametric polynomial r : ℕ → ℤ[X] with explicit values.

sections.title: Verification at p = 5
sections.summary: Proves r_5 has degree 2 and natDegree 2, is monic, and is Eisenstein at 5. The constant term 5 is not divisible by 25; the single sub-leading coefficient −5 is divisible by 5.
sections.mathContext: $r_5 = Y^2 - 5Y + 5$. Eisenstein at $p = 5$: leading 1 not in $(5)$, coefficient $-5 \in (5)$, constant $5 \notin (25)$.

sections.title: Verification at p = 7
sections.summary: Proves r_7 has degree 3 and natDegree 3, is monic, and is Eisenstein at 7. Three sub-leading coefficients (−7, 14, −7) all divisible by 7; constant term −7 not divisible by 49.
sections.mathContext: $r_7 = Y^3 - 7Y^2 + 14Y - 7$. Eisenstein at $p = 7$: leading 1, coefficients $(-7, 14, -7)$ all divisible by 7, constant $-7 \notin (49)$.

sections.title: Verification at p = 11
sections.summary: Proves r_11 has degree 5 and natDegree 5, is monic, and is Eisenstein at 11. Sub-leading coefficients (−11, 44, −77, 55, −11) all divisible by 11; constant term −11 not divisible by 121.

sections.title: Verification at p = 13
sections.summary: Proves r_13 has degree 6 and natDegree 6, is monic, and is Eisenstein at 13. Sub-leading coefficients (−13, 65, −156, 182, −91, 13) all divisible by 13; constant term 13 not divisible by 169.

sections.title: Four-Prime Verification, Packaged
sections.summary: Conjunction of the four per-prime IsEisensteinAt claims, packaged as `eisenstein_verified_small_primes`. Useful for downstream use and for documenting the empirical evidence behind the general conjecture.
sections.mathContext: $\forall p \in \{5, 7, 11, 13\}: r_p \text{ is Eisenstein at } p$.

sections.title: Irreducibility of r_{11} and r_{13}
sections.summary: Derives Irreducible (r 11) and Irreducible (r 13) by applying `Polynomial.irreducible_of_eisenstein_criterion`. The p=5 and p=7 cases are already established in sibling files via the same mechanism applied to the equivalent polynomials 4X²−2X−1 and 8X³−4X²−4X+1.
sections.mathContext: By Gauss's lemma and the integer-coefficient Eisenstein criterion, $r_{11}$ and $r_{13}$ are irreducible over $\mathbb{Z}$ (hence over $\mathbb{Q}$).

sections.title: Uniform Conjecture (Open)
sections.summary: States the general Eisenstein conjecture for cos(π/p) as `eisenstein_conjecture_cos_pi_p`, leaving the proof as a sorry. The proof outline (via Φ_{2p}(−1) = p and the local-field uniformizer theorem) is documented in the file comment and in knowledge.md.
sections.mathContext: $\forall p \geq 3 \text{ prime, } p \text{ odd}: \exists q \in \mathbb{Z}[X], \deg q = (p-1)/2 \wedge q \text{ monic} \wedge q.\mathrm{IsEisensteinAt}((p))$.
